# SID2XRNS dependency scope

SID2XRNS original code is AGPL-3.0-only; see `LICENSE`.

The CLI runtime vendors a five-module **ChiptuneSAK** subset from commit
`8759135b5c9c26dc9da155b006c575243ba5304a`, under the **MIT license**.
Only imports were made relative; emulator logic is unchanged. Copyright
2019-present David Youd and contributors. The exact license and original/adapted
file hashes are retained in `chiptunesak/LICENSE` and `chiptunesak/manifest.json`.
The original archive SHA-256 is
`4a4e0e012846a77fd5a38ee8e7eaa7e4e3c434f272393b765bb8dea59ea88a07`.
The converter CLI uses Python's standard library and has no other third-party runtime
package dependency. `sid2xrns/sidbus.py` implements the write-only SID bus policy
and model lifetimes described by **libresidfp 1.3.0**, commit
`5393471a02a505ff43aa710148b2d35289b72c31`, `src/SID.cpp` and `src/SID.h`.
This source is GPL-2.0-or-later; the GPLv3 option permits combination with this
project's AGPLv3 code. The pinned source credits Dag Lem, Antti Lankila and
Leandro Nini; its retained authors and license files are listed below. The core
is also used for optional bus-policy comparison, but is not a CLI binary or
runtime package dependency. See [the reference and check](../docs/TURRICAN.md).
`sid2xrns/envelope.py` ports the pinned core’s EnvelopeGenerator.h/.cpp
semantics, including LFSR and overlapping state/exponential/envelope pipelines,
under GPL-2.0-or-later (GPLv3 option for the AGPLv3 combination). Original
copyright: Leandro Nini (2011–2020), VICE Project (2018), Antti Lankila
(2007–2010), Dag Lem (2004, 2010). Licenses/authors remain below; exact
model hashes are in `docs/runtime-lock-v4.json`. No compiled core is required
by the CLI.

No C64 ROM, HVSC database or source SID music is bundled.
The original synthetic SID example is generated by this project's tests.

## Optional independent comparison environment

`bin/sid2xrns-compare` is separate from converter runtime. It uses the installed
**VICE VSID 3.10**, Arch package **vice 3.10-3**, as the independent CPU/PSID/reSID
reference. The exact executable/local-ROM hashes and analysis versions are in
`docs/reference-lock.json`. The installed package identifies **GPL-2.0-only**;
its unchanged metadata and license text are retained in `vice/package-desc.txt`
and `vice/GPL-2.0-only.txt`. The executable and ROMs are not redistributed.

Installed analysis packages are pinned to **NumPy 2.5.4**, **SciPy 1.18.1** and
**Matplotlib 3.11.2**. Their exact installed license/notice files, metadata and
hashes are retained under `analysis/` and `analysis/manifest.json`. NumPy declares
BSD-3-Clause AND 0BSD AND MIT AND Zlib AND CC0-1.0; SciPy's retained license is
BSD-style with its bundled notices; Matplotlib retains its Matplotlib/PSF-based
license agreement and historical notices. These packages are not bundled as
runtime binaries and were not installed/downloaded by this work.

The optional controlled-core renderer uses the already pinned **libresidfp
1.3.0** source/library and license below. It consumes independent VICE writes
or measured host writes; it is not a second independent sound-chip emulator.
See [COMPARISON.md](../docs/COMPARISON.md) for scope, clock conversion and limits.

The following notices were retained from the pinned SIDSynth source and apply
to the **optional real-processor timing probe**. The libresidfp source also
provides the bus-policy reference described above.
Their referenced license files and JUCE inventory remain intact.

# Third-party software

SIDSynth's original code is licensed under **AGPL-3.0-only**; see `LICENSE`.
The open-source JUCE license is selected. No commercial JUCE license is used.

| Dependency | Pinned source | License used |
| --- | --- | --- |
| JUCE 9.0.5 | [`d60b7a78030661574a615b586d9325ba7a7fa7dd`](https://github.com/juce-framework/JUCE/tree/d60b7a78030661574a615b586d9325ba7a7fa7dd) | AGPL-3.0-only |
| libresidfp 1.3.0 | [`5393471a02a505ff43aa710148b2d35289b72c31`](https://github.com/libsidplayfp/libresidfp/tree/5393471a02a505ff43aa710148b2d35289b72c31) | GPL-2.0-or-later, exercising the GPLv3 option for combination with AGPLv3 |
| VST3 SDK 3.8.0 | Vendored in the pinned JUCE source | MIT |

JUCE copyright: Raw Material Software Limited. Its exact license statement is
retained in `licenses/JUCE-LICENSE.md`. The full upstream dependency inventory,
including vendored versions, source locations and licenses, is retained in
`JUCE.spdx.json`. This inventory also lists JUCE components that SIDSynth does
not build or use. JUCE's modules retain their embedded third-party notices.

libresidfp copyright: Dag Lem (2000–2011), Antti Lankila (2007–2010), and Leandro
Nini (2010–2026). See `licenses/libresidfp-AUTHORS` and
`licenses/libresidfp-GPL-2.0.txt`. The GPLv3 text is retained as
`licenses/GPL-3.0.txt`; GPLv3 section 13 and AGPLv3 section 13 govern the
combination, with each component retaining its own license.

The Linux plugin's JUCE graphics/core dependencies include zlib 1.3.2 (Zlib),
HarfBuzz 15.0.0 (MIT), SheenBidi 2.9.0 (Apache-2.0), LunaSVG 3.5.0 and PlutoVG
1.3.2 (MIT), libpng 1.6.58 (libpng-2.0), Independent JPEG Group software 10.0
(IJG), and libwebp 1.6.0 (BSD-3-Clause). Their upstream license/notice files are
copied without modification beneath `licenses/juce-vendored/`, preserving source
paths. This software is based in part on the work of the Independent JPEG Group.
Additional embedded source notices remain in the pinned source distribution.

Stage 4 uses the MIDI keyboard in JUCE's `juce_audio_utils` module, which
also builds JUCE audio-format support. Its pinned-source inventory includes
FLAC 1.5.0, libogg 1.3.6, libvorbis 1.3.7, Opus 1.6.1,
opusfile 0.12-59-g6dfd29e and libopusenc 0.3 (BSD-3-Clause).
Their original notices are retained beneath
`licenses/juce-vendored/modules/juce_audio_formats/codecs/`. JUCE's built-in MP3,
WAV and AIFF implementations use JUCE's selected AGPL route. The plugin does
not offer a file player or open a separate audio device.

The SDK root, base, pluginterfaces and public.sdk MIT notices are retained.
VST is a trademark of Steinberg Media Technologies GmbH.

The build uses the system FreeType, Fontconfig, X11 and standard Linux runtime
libraries. These are system dependencies, not bundled copies. Web browser and
curl integration are disabled. No external SID player, C64 ROM, or musical data
is included.

`cmake/Dependencies.cmake` pins archive SHA-256 digests as well as source commits.
Its CMake adapter uses the libresidfp source list from the pinned `Makefile.am`
and configures its two generated headers with release settings. Stage 3 builds
from a separate source copy beneath the build tree and adds forward
`SidBackend` declarations and friend declarations to `SID.h` and
`WaveformGenerator.h`. The downloaded pinned source stays immutable.
`src/SidBackend.cpp` caches both models' existing
DAC/waveform tables and PAL/NTSC resamplers during construction/preparation,
then copies/swaps these configurations during playback without the allocation
and mutex in upstream's public setters. It also reseeds an all-zero noise
shift register when Noise alone is selected with TEST off, preventing a prior
combined waveform from leaving Noise permanently silent. This wrapper policy
preserves the oscillator accumulator, envelope, other voices and shared filter;
combined waveforms and healthy noise retain upstream behavior. Exactly one SID
core remains. Upstream emulation functions and license notices remain intact.
The adapter is tightly coupled to this pinned version and the configure step checks its patch
anchor; changes to upstream private fields require adapter review.
It does not use a system-installed, potentially different libresidfp.

Before distributing binaries, provide the corresponding SIDSynth source,
build files and these exact dependency sources under their respective licenses.
The local installation target includes the project license and retained notices.
